subject: Civil Engineering
title: Seismic Retrofitting
description: A quick, practical guide to Seismic Retrofitting.

hook.text: Millions of buildings were built before seismic codes existed. They're still standing — for now.

buildup.text: Retrofitting adds strength, stiffness, or ductility to existing buildings — a seismic upgrade.

discovery.text: Jacketing wraps columns in steel or concrete — increasing their shear and flexural capacity.

twist.text: Adding shear walls inside existing buildings is effective but changes the architecture.

climax.text: Los Angeles mandated retrofitting of 15,000 vulnerable buildings — the largest program ever.

punchline.text: You can't rebuild every old building. But you can make it survive the next earthquake.

quiz.question: What is column jacketing in seismic retrofitting?
options: Replacing old columns with entirely new, stronger ones
Wrapping existing columns in steel or concrete to increase their earthquake resistance
Covering columns with decorative material to hide seismic damage

details.summary: Seismic retrofitting strengthens existing buildings that were designed before modern seismic codes or to inadequate standards. Common techniques include adding shear walls, installing steel braces, wrapping columns with fiber-reinforced polymers, strengthening foundations.
details.whyItMatters: Most earthquake casualties occur in older buildings that predate seismic codes. Retrofitting the most vulnerable existing buildings is the most cost-effective way to reduce future earthquake deaths.
takeaways: Existing buildings often lack ductility required by modern seismic codes
Added shear walls and braces increase lateral strength and stiffness
Column wrapping with CFRP prevents brittle shear failure in concrete columns

faq.question: Which existing building types are most urgently in need of seismic retrofitting?
faq.answer: Unreinforced masonry buildings are the most vulnerable. Non-ductile concrete frame buildings with weak columns and strong beams collapse progressively. Soft-story buildings with open ground floors, such as apartment buildings with parking below, are prone to story collapse.

faq.question: How much does seismic retrofitting typically cost relative to building value?
faq.answer: Retrofit costs typically range from 5 to 30% of building replacement value, depending on the building type, deficiency level, and target performance. Basic life-safety retrofits cost less while immediate-occupancy performance requires more investment.
